classification.rationale: This is a podcast interview transcript featuring Nick Pope discussing his work at the UK Ministry of Defense's UFO desk. It contains anecdotal witness accounts (Cosford incident, art shop encounter) and personal recollections, but the primary source is a media interview, not an official document or direct witness testimony. The content is a mix of narrative and commentary, with no clear Hynek classification for a single observational event. The tone is conversational and public-facing.

_raw_list: Nick Pope worked at the UK Ministry of Defence UFO desk from 1991 to 1994, investigating UFO reports for defense, national security, and safety of flight implications.
The Cosford incident occurred on the night of March 30-31, 1993, involving a wave of sightings of a large triangular craft.
A civilian witness chased the triangular craft in his car while his family screamed at him to stop.
A farmer reported seeing the craft very low, possibly landing, and later found his cows standing in a circle facing each other, completely silent.
An Air Force witness reported the craft moving at 35-40 mph with a low-frequency humming sound, then accelerating to the horizon instantly without a sonic boom.
Radar data from the Cosford incident was inconclusive, with some uncorrelated targets but not definitive.

A woman running an art shop in central London reported a group of normal-looking people who bought a single pencil with a high-denomination banknote and seemed confused by the concept of receiving change.
The same woman later reported a time slip experience, missing time, and seeing someone who looked like herself from the future.
Nick Pope states that he self-censored in official reports, focusing on pilot sightings and radar cases while downplaying abduction and high-strangeness cases.
Nick Pope claims the UFO-to-UAP rebranding was partly to shed pop culture baggage and secure congressional funding.
